explanation.text: The mole was retained as an SI base unit for amount of substance following the 2019 revision of the International System of Units.
The 2019 redefinition of the SI base units revised the definition of the mole but did not remove it from the list of base units.
The mole is defined as the SI unit of amount of substance with the symbol mol under the 2019 definition.
The revision of the SI that took effect on 20 May 2019 included a new definition of the mole based on a fixed number of elementary entities.
The mole remained one of the seven SI base units after the 2019 redefinition, as confirmed by the official SI Brochure.

excerpts.text: Relative atomic masses Metrologia Amount of substance and the mole in the SI Bernd Güttler1, Horst Bettin1, Richard J C Brown2 , Richard S Davis3 , Zoltan Mester4 , Martin J T Milton3 , Axel Pramann1 , Olaf Rienitz1 , Robert D Vocke5 and Robert I Wielgosz3 1 Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB), Bundesallee 100, 38116 Braunschweig, Germany 2 National Physical Laboratory (NPL), Hampton Road, Teddington, Middlesex, TW11 0LW, United Kingdom 3 Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (BIPM), Pavillon de Breteuil, F-92312 Sèvres CEDEX, France 4 National Research Council Canada (NRC), 1200 Montreal Road, Ottawa, Ontario K1A 0R6, Canada 5 National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), 100 Bureau Drive, Gaithersburg, MD 20899, United States of America E-mail: bernd.guettler@ptb.de Received 2 February 2019, revised 24 April 2019 Accepted for publication 7 May 2019 Published 3 June 2019 Abstract Following the revision of the International System of Units (SI), that takes effect on 20 May 2019, the unit mole is defined by using a fixed number of elementary entities.
